title: Human Islet Isolation Media Preparation
author: James Lyon
materials: Prepare the HBSS, M199, and EMEM solutions outlined in step 1 of the Stock Media Preparation table using the following directions: Dispense 9 L of Milli-Q (18mΩ) water in to the carboy Store overnight at 4 °C to allow to come to temperature. Using the stirrer add the media powder to the water and allow to go into solution. Add the powdered supplements and Penicillin/Streptomycin to the appropriate media based on the above tables and allow to stir into solution. Stir the solution for 00:30:00 Store the prepared solution overnight at 4 °C to allow all powders to go into solution Stir the solution for 00:30:00 Calibrate the pH meter using the pH control buffers Adjust the pH level to pH 7.4 using the NaOH and/or HCl solutions. Bring to volume with the appropriate amount of Milli-Q water.

steps.title: Filter media with peristaltic pump
steps.instruction: Connect silicon 25‑gauge tubing and a nylon capsule filter (0.22 µm membrane) to the peristaltic pump and filter the prepared media into a sterilized media bottle; store the filtered media at 4 °C until needed for supplementation prior to isolation.

steps.title: Prepare base media solution
steps.instruction: Make a 1 L media solution by dissolving the reagent powder in Milli‑Q water, adjusting pH, and filter‑sterilizing.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 0.9 L of Milli‑Q water into a carboy and store overnight at 4 °C to allow the water to reach room temperature.
Using a magnetic stirrer, add the reagent powder to the water according to the table referenced as Step 4 and stir for 00:30:00.
Calibrate the pH meter with pH control buffers, then adjust the solution to pH 7.4 using NaOH and/or HCl as needed.
Bring the solution to a final volume of 1 L with additional Milli‑Q water.
Filter‑sterilize the completed solution through a bottle‑top filter (0.22 µm) into a sterile 1 L bottle.

steps.title: Prepare dithizone staining solution
steps.instruction: Make a dithizone stock solution and use it to stain islet suspensions.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 0.2 g of dithizone powder into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 6 mL of DMSO and mix until the powder is fully dissolved.
Bring the solution to a total volume of 40 mL with HBSS and mix.
Transfer the dithizone solution to a 60 mL syringe fitted with a 0.45 µm nylon filter.
For staining, add an equal volume of the dithizone solution to each mL of islet suspension (e.g., 100 µL islet suspension + 100 µL dithizone + 200 µL HBSS for visualization).
If desired, add an additional 2 mL of HBSS to each stained sample to dilute the stain and reduce background colour.

steps.title: Prepare working solution supplements
steps.instruction: Add the indicated supplements to each stock media according to the detailed table.

substeps.instruction: Media Total per bottle – BSA 25%: add 1172 µL, 160 µL (4.0 %), 1000 µL; prepare 12 aliquots of M199.
Dilution #1, #2, #3 – add 2020 µL (x3) and 2000 µL (x3); add 20 µL priming solution.
Priming solution – add 1000 µL and another 1000 µL as indicated.
Wash 1 (split into 2 × 550 mL): add 1105 µL (x1) and 95 µL (2.5 %); add 1000 µL; final volume 10 mL.
Wash 2 – add 1055 µL (x5) and 45 µL (1.125 %); add 1000 µL (x5); final volume 10 mL.
Cannulation – add 500 µL and another 500 µL as indicated.
Perfusion Solution – add 350 µL and another 350 µL as indicated.
Decon 1 – add 250 µL and 200 µL Betadine (50 mL).
Decon 2 – add 250 µL and 250 µL.
Decon 3 – add 250 µL and 250 µL.
Gradient Collection Tubes – for tubes 1‑6 add wash solution volumes: 100 µL, 150 µL, 200 µL, 200 µL, 225 µL, 225 µL; for tubes 7‑12 add: 225 µL, 225 µL, 225 µL, 225 µL, 225 µL, 150 µL.

steps.title: Prepare human islet culture media
steps.instruction: Supplement CMRL medium with the components listed in the accompanying table, then filter‑sterilize the final solution through a 0.22 µm Stericup sterile vacuum filtration system.

steps.title: Prepare density gradients
steps.instruction: Create high‑ and low‑density gradients using Bicoll and UW solution according to the specified volumes and target densities.

substeps.instruction: High density gradient: combine 77 µL Bicoll (1.100 g/mL) with 64 µL UW solution (1.042 g/mL) to obtain 141 µL at a final density of 1.074 g/mL.
Low density gradient: combine 52 µL Bicoll with 88 µL UW solution to obtain 140 µL at a final density of 1.064 g/mL.
